methodological_rigor.justification: The study is a large single-institution retrospective cohort of 659 EC patients from 1989-2022 with AI-quantified TILs on HE slides, MMR IHC, and Cox proportional hazards modeling, which is appropriate for the research question. Strengths include exploratory analyses of three candidate annotation areas, sensitivity analyses over alternative cutoffs (quartiles, median), AIC/BIC model comparisons, and pre-specified subgroup analyses by histological subtype and MMR status. Important limitations acknowledged by the authors weaken rigor: no external validation cohort, training set of only 2235 lymphocytes from four cases without stratification by subtype, manual invasive-frontline annotation with no inter-observer reproducibility assessment, no POLE genotyping, and a ROC AUC of only 0.570 for recurrence/progression, indicating modest discrimination of the dichotomized classifier. Backward stepwise selection of multivariate covariates on the same data used for discovery also risks optimism bias.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual retrospective cohort study evaluating a prognostic biomarker in EC, mapping to Oxford LoE 2b. TIL-based risk stratification is clinically plausible and aligns with molecular-classification trends in EC, and HR 0.61 for PFS and 0.54 for OS are clinically meaningful effects. However, the absence of external validation, modest AUC (0.570), and lack of integration with the established molecular classes (POLE, p53, MMR, NSMP) limits immediate practice-changing impact; the authors frame the work as hypothesis-generating requiring further validation.

reporting_quality.justification: As a prognostic biomarker study REMARK is the most applicable standard. The manuscript reports cohort definition, inclusion/exclusion, endpoints, IHC scoring rules, and multivariable modeling, but several REMARK items are incomplete: no flow of patients (CONSORT/REMARK-style diagram), no sample-size justification, no explicit handling of missing data, no report of proportional-hazards assumption checks, and no pre-specification of the TIL cutoff (the ROC-derived cutoff is data-driven). Data availability is weak with no mention of a deposited digital-slide dataset, classifier weights, or code; only supplementary figures/tables are referenced.

novelty_literature.justification: TIL quantification as a prognostic marker in EC is well established, and AI-based TIL quantification has been reported in ovarian HGSC (reference 23 by a closely related author group), breast, and other cancers. The novelty here lies in the specific application to EC around the invasive frontline using HALO/Object Phenotyper with a 500 um span and in pairing AI-TIL with MMR IHC. This represents a meaningful extension of prior work to a new disease site rather than a methodological first or a mechanistic breakthrough.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is generally clear and organized along standard IMRaD lines, with figure callouts, a limitations paragraph, and defined statistical conventions. However the ROC AUC is reported inconsistently (0.570 in the Results text versus 0.573 in Figure 4 caption), the Methods describe three candidate annotation areas but citation of literature (reference 21) for the rationale appears to point to an esophageal study rather than an EC study, and some sentences are long and repetitive (especially the limitations/future-work paragraph). Tables and figures are not shown inline, so content must be inferred from captions.

key_strengths: Large single-institution cohort (n=659) with long follow-up (median 63 months) and consistently defined PFS/OS endpoints.
Pre-specified exploratory analyses of three annotation geometries and sensitivity analyses over multiple cutoffs with AIC/BIC model comparison.

Integration of AI-quantified TILs with MMR IHC and subgroup analyses by histological aggressiveness and MMR status, with biologically consistent findings (higher TILs in dMMR, earlier stage, less deep myometrial invasion).
F1 score of 0.81 for lymphocyte detection, within the range reported in prior AI-TIL literature.
key_concerns: ROC AUC of only 0.570 (or 0.573 per Figure 4) indicates weak discrimination of the dichotomized High/Low-TIL classifier, tempering prognostic utility claims.
No external or multi-institutional validation cohort; all modeling, cutoff selection, and multivariable variable selection occur in the same dataset, raising optimism bias.
Classifier training used only 2235 lymphocytes from four cases and did not stratify by histological subtype, limiting generalizability.
POLE status, a pillar of modern EC molecular classification, was not evaluated, so the AI-TIL signal is not contextualized within the established ProMisE/TCGA subtypes.
Invasive-frontline annotation was manual with no inter-observer reproducibility assessment, and discrepant AUC values (0.570 vs 0.573) suggest minor reporting inconsistencies.
REMARK-style reporting is incomplete (no patient-flow diagram, no sample-size justification, no proportional-hazards check, no code or data availability statement).
chief_reviewer.rationale: The study is a competent, well-motivated single-center AI-pathology cohort study with meaningful HRs but modest discrimination and no external validation. It fits Tier 3 (e.g., Cancers, BMC Cancer class) with major revisions to strengthen validation, REMARK reporting, and integration with molecular classification.
